questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: In the 1920s, Otto Warburg observed that cancerous cells consume a lot of glucose and produce a lot of lactate even in the presence of sufficient oxygen. This effect observed in cancerous cells is also referred to as:

options.label: D
options.text: Inhibition of oxygen uptake by glycolysis

questions.solutionHtml:
Aerobic glycolysis
  • In cancer cells, pyruvate is converted to lactate even in the presence of O2. This is known as the Warburg effect or aerobic glycolysis.
  • Lactic acid makes the local environment acidic helping in metastasis.
  • Energy derived from the conversion of pyruvate to lactate is just 2 ATPs, so, cancer cells take up a large amount of glucose compared to normal cells.
  • This leads to glucose wastage by cells and weight loss (cachexia).



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 704

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: The polyol pathway plays an important role in meeting the energy requirements of seminal vesicles because it is responsible for the formation of which of following:
questions.solutionHtml:
Fructose from glucose
  • This is a short pathway to synthesize fructose in the body via sorbitol. First glucose is reduced to its alcohol i.e. sorbitol (or glucitol) by the enzyme aldose reductase (the same enzyme which reduces galactose to galactitol).
  • Then sorbitol is oxidized to fructose by the enzyme sorbitol dehydrogenase.
  • This synthesis of fructose in the body is especially useful in seminal vesicles for sperms as they mainly use fructose as the source of energy.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 197

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: Net ATPs produced by when one molecule of fructose is converted to two molecules of pyruvate?
questions.solutionHtml:
2
  • The ATP yield of fructose is the same as that of glucose.
  • One may argue that fructose enters glycolysis bypassing the energy investment step (fructose-1-phosphate to fructose 1,6 bisphosphate) and thus 1 ATP should be obtained extra. but one extra ATP is used for the conversion of glyceraldehyde to GAP. So, ATP consumption (total 2 per fructose) is the same as glycolysis of glucose.
  • Look at the ATP used in kinase reaction in the image when fructose enters glycolysis.

Hence Net ATP yield is also 4 ATP produced- 2 ATP used = 2 ATPs





Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 197

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about the metabolism of carbohydrates is correct?

options.label: B
options.text: Fructose is an aldose sugar like glucose.

options.label: C
options.text: Fructose transport into cells is insulin dependent.

options.label: D
options.text: Galactose is phosphorylated to galactose-1-phosphate by galactokinase

questions.answerText: Galactose is phosphorylated to galactose-1-phosphate by galactokinase
questions.solutionHtml:
Galactose is phosphorylated to galactose-1-phosphate by galactokinase
  • Galactokinase catalyzes the first step of galactose breakdown.
  • It catalyzes the phosphorylation of the C1 alcohol group of galactose to produce galactose-1-phosphate.
  • The deficiency of this enzyme results in the accumulation of galactose and is known as minor type galactosemia.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 198

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: Snowflake cataract is produced because of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Aldose reductase
  • In diabetics, excess glucose freely enters the cells of the eye which are highly permeable to glucose.
  • Here, glucose is reduced by the aldose reductase enzyme to produce sorbitol/polyol.
  • In other cells, this sorbitol is oxidized to keto sugar fructose by the enzyme sorbitol dehydrogenase, but this enzyme is absent in the eye, hence sorbitol accumulation occurs.
  • Sorbitol is hygroscopic in nature and absorbs water causing swelling of the cells.
  • Swelling due to excess sorbitol in the lens ultimately leads to snowflake cataract.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 200

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: Essential pentosuria is due to a deficiency of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Xylulose reductase
  • Essential Pentosuria can occur due to a deficiency of either of these two enzymes:

Xylulose reductase

Xylitol dehydrogenase

  • These enzymes are part of minor pathways of glucose oxidation known as the uronic acid pathway (see attached treasure)
  • Diagnostic features:
    • L-xylulose accumulates and comes out in urine, which gives a positive Benedict’s test as it is a reducing sugar, but the glucose oxidase test strip is negative.
    • Symptoms appear due to the consumption of a large amount of fruits that are rich in pentoses.
  • It is a part of Garrod's tetrad (see attached treasure)



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 198

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stemHtml: What is the enzyme involved in the following conversion?
questions.solutionHtml:
Aldose reductase
  • Monosaccharides get converted to their respective alcohols on reduction.
  • Glucose gets converted to its alcohol i.e. sorbitol.
  • Galactose is converted to its alcohol i.e. galactitol.
  • In both cases, a common enzyme aldose reductase is used (see fig.)




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 197

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: Familial fructokinase deficiency causes no symptoms because:

options.label: C
options.text: Excess fructose does not escape into the urine

options.label: D
options.text: Excess fructose is excreted through feces

questions.solutionHtml:
Hexokinase can phosphorylate fructose

Fructose metabolism

  • Fructokinase is the first enzyme for fructose metabolism and it converts fructose to fructose-1-P.
  • In Fructokinase deficiency,
    • Hexokinase (a non-specific enzyme) can phosphorylate fructose and glucose but it has a low affinity (high km) for fructose.
    • Glucose is the true substrate for hexokinase.
  • Fructose-6-phosphate formed by hexokinase reaction can enter the glycolytic pathway, so, it does not accumulate to produce toxic effects.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 199-200

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stemHtml: A 58-year-old man with type I (IDDM) diabetes went to an ophthalmologist for an assessment of developing a cataract. The results of his blood work are shown below:Which of the following enzymes is most strongly associated with cataract formation in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Aldose reductase
  • The blood examination with high fasting glucose (>126 mg/dl) and HBA1c >6.5% along with urine ketone bodies and urine glucose indicate a diabetic condition.
  • In diabetic patients, excess blood glucose enters insulin-insensitive tissues and leads to the formation of sorbitol by aldose reductase. But sorbitol dehydrogenase is absent in most of these cells and sorbitol cannot be converted to fructose. Hence, sorbitol accumulation occurs.
  • As sorbitol is hygroscopic and will absorb water causing cell swelling ultimately leading to snowflake cataract in diabetic patients (see fig).




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 200

questions.stem: Biological dehydrogenation reactions are enzyme-catalyzed oxidation-reduction reactions where one molecule loses hydrogen or electrons and other molecule accept it. Most of the time the cofactor of the enzyme plays a role as an electron acceptor or donor. Which vitamin as a coenzyme is required for glucose 6 phosphate dehydrogenase?
questions.solutionHtml:
Niacin
  • Niacin is a pyridine derivative.
  • Coenzyme forms: NADP+, NAD+
  • These coenzyme forms are involved in a variety of oxidation-reduction reactions as a part of oxidoreductases enzymes e.g. (see table below)

Enzyme

Isocitrate dehydrogenase

NAD+

NADP+

NAD+

Glutamate dehydrogenase

NAD+

Lactate dehydrogenase

NAD+

NAD+




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 193

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: Patient of 34 years of age was reported in the hospital with complaints of fatigue, dizziness, nausea, and headache past 4 days. Upon examination, pallor was noted in the conjunctiva, palm, and nail beds. The liver is tender and palpable. History of the patient revealed intake of a fixed-dose combination of trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole (Septran DS) 10 days earlier on the prescription of a physician for treatment of sore throat. Microscopic blood examination indicates a nonspherocytic and normocytic anemia which most probably is a due reduction in the synthesis of:
questions.solutionHtml:
NADPH
  • The patient has glucose 6-P dehydrogenase deficiency and cannot generate NADPH from glucose 6-P. In the red blood cells, which lack mitochondria, this is the only pathway through which NADPH can be generated.
  • In the absence of NADPH, the molecule which protects against oxidative damage (glutathione) is oxidized preferentially to protect membrane lipids and proteins.
  • There is only limited glutathione in the membrane, so once it is oxidized, it needs to be converted back to reduced glutathione (the protective form).
  • The enzyme that does this, glutathione reductase, requires NADPH to supply the electrons to reduce the oxidized glutathione.

In the absence of NADPH, the glutathione cannot be reduced (Option D is false), and the protection offered by reduced glutathione is eliminated, leading to membrane damage and cell lysis.





Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 194-195

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: The HMP pathway consists of two phases known as oxidative and non-oxidative phases. The oxidation of glucose by this pathway produces which of the following as final products?
questions.solutionHtml:
6 NADPH
  • In the oxidative phase, 2 NADPH are produced from 1 glucose molecule to give a final product of ribulose-5-P.
  • Now to complete the non-oxidative phase, at least three molecules of ribulose-5-P need to enter this phase (see fig in treasure attached).
  • To form three ribulose-5-P, 3 glucose 6-P will need to be oxidized initially out of which 2 molecules are recovered again at the end.
  • Hence, the total reaction of HMP pathway can be written as:
  • So, in net reaction, a single molecule of glucose is broken into glyceraldehyde-3-P and 3 CO2 and 6 NADPH
  • or, for a complete cycle with 3glucose-6-P molecules, 6NADPH are produced
  • Or we can say, the final products of HMP are 6NADPH.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 191-193

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: An infant of age 8 months was taken to the clinic of a pediatrician. The infant was restless and crying. Vomitus was noted on the clothes of the infant. Parents gave a history of periodic abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea that started after the weaning of the nfant with fruit juices and corn syrup past month. Upon physical examination, hepatomegaly was evident. Laboratory investigation revealed the presence of reducing sugar upon analysis by the Seliwanoff reagent. Select the deficient enzyme in the body of the infant under the above-mentioned clinical manifestations?
questions.solutionHtml:
Aldolase B deficiency

The deficiency of aldolase B results in failure to split fructose-1-phosphate into DHAP and glyceraldehyde 3P. As a result, fructose 1P accumulates in body tissues involving irreversible injury to the liver (hepatomegaly). This condition is called hereditary fructose intolerance, which is a severe form of disorder requiring medical attention. Fructose can be estimated in urine by the Seliwanoff test that is meant for ketohexose only.




Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 101,138

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: Hexose monophosphate (HMP) shunt is an alternative pathway for the oxidation of glucose mainly used for the synthesis of NADPH and ribose 5-P required in synthetic reactions. The number of ATPs produced by HMP shunt is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Zero

HMP shunt/ Pentose Phosphate pathway

  • It is one of the alternative pathways to glycolysis for glucose utilization.
  • It neither produces nor utilizes ATPs (see attached treasure).
  • 2 main products of HMP shunt are:
    • NADPH → in the irreversible oxidative phase
    • Ribose-5-phosphate → in reversible non-oxidative phase



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 199

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stemHtml: Identify A and B enzymes in the given figure:
questions.solutionHtml:
Glutathione peroxidase and Glutathione reductase
  • In RBCs, HMP forms NADPH. It is used to reduce oxidized glutathione and, in the process, itself gets oxidized (removal of hydrogen) to NADP. The enzyme involved is glutathione reductase, which requires FAD (or Vit B2).
  • So, the function of HMP in RBCs is to produce this reduced glutathione which is used to destroy H2O2.
  • Now glutathione gets oxidized again by the reduction of H2O2 to harmless water. The enzyme involved is glutathione peroxidase, which is a selenoprotein (requires selenocysteine, the 21st amino acid at its active site).




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 195

questions.topic: eGurukul · HMP, Metabolism of Galactose & Fructose
questions.stem: An infant of age 4 months is breastfeeding. Suddenly, the infant developed disliking to feed, vomiting, and restlessness. The body weight of infant started to decline. The parents brought the infant to the pediatrician for consultation. Upon examination, the physician observed hepatomegaly, jaundice, and bilateral cataract. Select the deficient enzyme responsible for the clinical manifestations in the infant?
questions.solutionHtml:
Deficiency of galactose-1-phosphate uridyl transferase
  • Galactose is produced in the intestine from the degradation of milk sugar lactose by the enzyme lactase.
  • The patient’s symptoms suggest it to be a case of classic galactosemia which is due to a deficiency of enzyme Galactose 1-phosphate uridyltransferase of galactose metabolism.
  • Excess Gal accumulation occurs in this disease in the liver causing jaundice, vomiting, hepatomegaly, and in the brain causing mental retardation.
  • Other clinical features include a high risk of E.coli sepsis (reason unknown) and Oil-drop cataract due to inhibition of galactokinase by product inhibition as shown in the figure in the text.




Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 137,140
